case.question: Why would an induction motor not start when given a command signal, even though the drive shows no fault code?

key_points: Control signal source may be wired incorrectly or not active
Motor nameplate FLA may exceed drive current rating, causing startup current limit
Mechanical load binding or jam prevents acceleration
Enable or run permissive input (safety circuit, interlock) may not be satisfied
wrong_if: Assumes the motor winding is open without checking control wiring first
Claims DC bus voltage automatically resets if the motor doesn't start within 5 seconds
States that a missing start signal is always a PLC programming error, not a wiring issue

turns.question: Why would an induction motor not start when given a command signal, even though the drive shows no fault code?
turns.answer:
Most often, the drive is seeing the command but is still inhibited by an enable/interlock, reference, or start-permit condition, so it never actually applies output to the motor. Other common causes are no valid speed reference, local/remote control mismatch, safety circuit open, motor wiring issue, incorrect motor data, or a mechanical load that is jammed or too heavy to start. If the drive has no fault code, that usually means it is not seeing a hard electrical trip; it does **not** mean the motor is being driven.

If you want, I can help you narrow it down by the exact drive status indications: is it showing “ready/running,” and do you hear the contactor or see any output current when the start command is given?
